title: Human Digestive System
seo_title: Secondary 2 Science: Human Digestive System Worksheets (Lower Secondary Science with Answers)
standard_text: Explain the importance of the digestive system; explain how the mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum and anus work together; describe how food is digested, including carbohydrases, proteases and lipases, and that the products are used for respiration, growth and repair; appreciate food and lifestyle choices in fighting diabetes; recognise helpful and harmful bacteria in the gut (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 science worksheets for Singapore students on the human digestive system: organs and their jobs, physical and chemical digestion, enzymes and absorption. With answers.
key_big: Digestion makes food small enough to absorb.
key_sub: Absorbed in the small intestine; water absorbed in the large intestine.
body_html:
How to think about it

Digestion breaks large food molecules into small, soluble ones that can be absorbed into the blood.

  • Path: mouth → gullet → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum → anus.
  • Physical digestion: teeth, churning, bile. Chemical digestion: enzymes.
  • Carbohydrase: starch → sugars. Protease: proteins → amino acids. Lipase: fats → fatty acids and glycerol.
  • The small intestine absorbs digested food; the large intestine absorbs water.
Example

Which enzyme digests proteins, and into what?

Name from the food

Answer: protease, into amino acids

Example

Where is most digested food absorbed?

Large surface area

Answer: the small intestine

Common mistakes

  • Saying digestion is finished in the stomach. It is completed in the small intestine.
  • Saying the large intestine absorbs most food. It absorbs mainly water.
  • Calling enzymes living things. They are proteins.
  • Calling bile an enzyme. It only breaks fat into droplets.
